raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Addresses #59054 for the non-DiffKV kernel (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_unified_attention.py`).

Speculative-decode verify batches (`max_seqlen_q = 1 + k`) are kept off the split-KV 3D path by the `max_seqlen_q > 1` term of the launch gate. For one sequence, the 2D grid is `(total_num_q_blocks, num_kv_heads)`, which is a handful of programs, and each one walks the whole KV history. On long contexts this dominates the step time.

This PR:

1. **Adds `VLLM_TRITON_3D_MAX_Q`** (default `1`, which keeps today's behaviour). Queries with `max_seqlen_q <= VLLM_TRITON_3D_MAX_Q` may take the 3D path, provided the total token count fits the segment scratch (`q.shape[0] <= seq_threshold_3D`). The scratch buffers are indexed by token, and `reduce_segments` already runs per token.
2. **Guards fully masked segments.** With several query tokens per program, a row can have every key of a segment masked. This happens when a segment boundary sits just before the last query tokens. The online-softmax update then ends at `M = 0, L = 0`, and the epilogue would store `M = 0` as that segment's maximum. When the real maxima are strongly negative, `reduce_segments` underflows every real segment and the row comes out wrong. The epilogue now stores `-inf` when `L == 0`. The same idea is used for DiffKV in #59085.
3. **Clamps an all-`-inf` `overall_max` to 0** in `reduce_segments`, so a row with no visible key yields 0 instead of NaN. This is the same line as in #58141.

### Why this is not a duplicate

- #44652, #45450 and #52879 relax the same gate for this kernel, each with a different admission policy (constant, spec-config-derived, capacity-derived).
- None of them includes the per-row masked-segment guard (2). Without it, admitting multi-token queries to 3D produces wrong attention outputs. The new test `test_spec_verify_3d_fully_masked_segment_rows` fails if either (2) or (3) is removed.
- #59085 and #58141 only touch the DiffKV kernel.
- If maintainers prefer one of the open gate PRs, I am happy to close this one, provided the guard and the test are carried over. I posted the same analysis on #59054.

### AI assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). That covers the root-cause analysis, the patch, the tests and the benchmarks. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and benchmarks below on my own hardware.

## Test Plan

```
pytest -q tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py -k spec_verify
```

- `test_spec_verify_3d_matches_reference` checks the 3D path against a dense PyTorch reference. It covers bf16 and fp8 KV, block sizes 16 and 1600, `q_len` 2 and 4, and sequence lengths 37 to 32768.
- `test_spec_verify_3d_fully_masked_segment_rows` sweeps sequence lengths 1 to 199 at `q_len=4` with strongly negative logits. It covers rows with a fully masked segment (epilogue guard) and rows with no visible key at all, `seq_len < q_len` (reducer clamp).
- End-to-end serving with MTP, stock vs. `VLLM_TRITON_3D_MAX_Q=4`. Identical prompts (fixed seed), prefix caching off, greedy decoding, with a comparison of the generated text.

## Test Result

**Hardware:**
- AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Strix Halo), Radeon 8060S **gfx1151** (40 CUs, ~256 GB/s).
- `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.30.0`, torch 2.12, HIP 7.2, Triton 3.7.1.
- The patch applies cleanly to both v0.30.0 and `main`.

**Unit tests:** `-k spec_verify`: 25 passed. Ablation (thanks to @hclsys, who also reproduced 242/242 on GB10 / sm_121 with the earlier test):

| guards | result |
|---|---|
| both | 25 passed |
| reducer clamp (3) removed | 1 failed |
| epilogue guard (2) removed | 1 failed |
| neither | 1 failed |

Existing 3D-path tests, stock kernel vs. this PR (default `VLLM_TRITON_3D_MAX_Q=1`): all `seq_threshold_3D=8`, `num_blocks=2048` cases of `test_triton_unified_attention.py`. That is 468 tests across `test_triton_unified_attn`, `_bf16_query_fp8_kv`, `_fp16_input_fp8_output` and `_use_td`, with **468 passed on both**.

**Kernel** (Qwen3.8-27B full-attention shape: 24 Q / 4 KV heads, head 256, fp8 KV, block 1600, one sequence, per call):

| KV len | q_len | stock (ms) | this PR (ms) | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4096 | 1 | 0.101 | 0.102 | 1.0x |
| 4096 | 4 | 2.959 | 0.572 | 5.2x |
| 16384 | 4 | 9.011 | 0.731 | 12.3x |
| 32768 | 4 | 72.199 | 2.773 | 26.0x |
| 65536 | 4 | 262.769 | 5.392 | 48.7x |

**Serving.** Qwen3.8-27B W4A16 (hybrid GDN + 16 full-attention layers), MTP `num_speculative_tokens=3`, `TRITON_ATTN`, fp8 KV, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graphs. Steady-state decode after a 32k-token prompt, measured on 160 generated tokens and skipping the first 5 steps:

| config | step time | tokens / step | decode |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| MTP, stock | 581 ms | 3.2 | ~5.5 tok/s |
| MTP, this PR | 162 ms | 3.3 | **~20.5 tok/s (3.7x)** |
| no speculative decoding | 92 ms | 1.0 | 10.9 tok/s |

At 32k, speculative decoding goes from a 2x loss to a 1.9x gain over no-spec. Results are identical with `PIECEWISE` CUDA graphs (163 ms/step). Prefill (TTFT) is unchanged: it stays on the 2D path.

**Outputs.** Greedy, identical prompts, stock vs. this PR, from 512 to 32k tokens. 7 of 11 completions are byte-identical. The others diverge into equally plausible continuations (for example `bytearray()` vs `b''` in generated code), which is consistent with near-tie flips from the different reduction order. We saw no degenerate output. MTP acceptance was unchanged or higher on the long-context cases.

Ran this on a DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121, CUDA 13) as a second platform for your gfx1151 numbers. **242 passed**, same as yours. Both guards are right and the gate default keeps today's behaviour.

One gap: **your test covers one of the two guards.** Ablating them separately:

```
both guards                        242 passed
reducer clamp removed              242 passed      <- not covered
epilogue -inf guard removed          1 failed, 241 passed
```

The clamp isn't redundant though — it's just unreachable from the sweep. `test_spec_verify_3d_masked_segment_sweep` runs `range(8, 521)` with `q_len=4`, so `context_len = seq_len - q_len >= 4` and every query row always sees at least one key. Going below that through your own `_run`:

```
q_len = 4, both guards        kv_len 1 2 3 4 5 8  ->  no NaN anywhere
q_len = 4, clamp removed      kv_len 1 2 3        ->  NaN
                              kv_len 4 5 8        ->  clean
```

So `kv_len < q_len` is the shape that needs it, and the sweep starts one step above it. Lowering the bound (or just adding `[1]` to the multi-sequence `seq_lens` set) would pin the clamp too — worth it because the clamp is the one that *looks* redundant next to the epilogue guard, so it's the one someone simplifies away later.

**Same pair, same order, on the DiffKV kernel.** #58141 carries the clamp and #59085 carried only the epilogue guard; on my card #59085 NaN'd at `q=8, kv_len=1` and `kv_len=3` until it picked up #58141's clamp, at which point those rows went to 0 and matched the 2D path exactly. Identical failure shape to what I just measured here, in the other file.

That's now five open PRs relaxing this gate across two kernels — #44652, #45450, #52879, yours here, and #58141/#59085 on the DiffKV side. Whichever combination lands, **both** guards need to survive, and only two of those five currently have the pair. Your closing note says #59448 can be dropped in favour of whichever lands "as long as the guard and the test are carried over" — I'd say that more strongly: it's two guards, and the test as written only proves one of them.

Thanks, that ablation is exactly the gap. Fixed in 06189c4: the sweep now starts at `seq_len=1`, so `seq_len < q_len` rows (no visible key at all) are covered, and the reference expects 0 for them. Re-running your ablation on gfx1151:

| guards | `-k spec_verify` |
|---|---|
| both | 25 passed |
| reducer clamp removed | 1 failed |
| epilogue `-inf` guard removed | 1 failed |
| neither | 1 failed |

Agreed on the stronger wording: it is both guards, and each one now has a failing test without it. Thanks also for the GB10 run.

Reran the ablation on sm_121 against 06189c4, same table as your gfx1151 run:

```
both guards                 25 passed
reducer clamp removed        1 failed
epilogue -inf guard removed  1 failed
neither                      1 failed
```

Coverage gap's closed on both arches. Nothing further from me.

I ran this on gfx1201 too (one Radeon AI PRO R9700), in case another arch helps. Stock v0.31.1rc0 plus this PR at `2c23f722` (applies cleanly), ROCm 10.0, torch 2.13, Triton 3.8.0.

`-k spec_verify`: 25 passed. The ablation reproduces here as well: dropping the epilogue guard, the reducer clamp, or both fails `test_spec_verify_3d_fully_masked_segment_rows` (1 failed, 24 passed). The rest of the file at the default `VLLM_TRITON_3D_MAX_Q=1` is 1879 passed on stock and the same 1879 with the PR.

Kernel, same shape as your table (24 Q / 4 KV heads, head 256, fp8 KV, block 1600, one sequence, 16 segments), median of 50 calls:

| KV len | q_len | stock (ms) | this PR (ms) | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4096 | 4 | 0.329 | 0.098 | 3.4x |
| 16384 | 4 | 1.201 | 0.220 | 5.5x |
| 32768 | 4 | 2.448 | 0.407 | 6.0x |
| 65536 | 2 | 5.016 | 0.779 | 6.4x |
| 65536 | 4 | 5.106 | 0.816 | 6.3x |
| 65536 | 5 | 5.074 | 1.176 | 4.3x |
| 65536 | 8 | 5.069 | 1.614 | 3.1x |
| 65536 | 1 | 0.539 | 0.548 | 1.0x |

Max |3D − 2D| on the same inputs is 4.9e-4 (bf16 out), the same as stock's q_len 1 path. The gain is smaller than on your gfx1151 because stock 2D doesn't fall off as hard on this card (5.1 ms at 64k vs your 263 ms), but it's still 3-6x everywhere I measured.

I've been running a similar local change (verify batches into 3D) on two R9700s since late August, with DFlash2 at 4 draft tokens. It doesn't have your masked-segment guard, which the ablation shows is needed, so +1 to getting this in with the test. (#59054 was closed by #59085, but that only covers the DiffKV kernel.)

AI assistance (Claude) was used to run these measurements and draft this comment.

Thanks for the gfx1201 run and the timings, good to see the 3-6x hold on a third arch.

One update since your run: cce2aaa fixes a sliding-window case raised in review (a fully masked first tile leaving a stale maximum), with a new test. It doesn't change the full-attention path you measured.

Re-ran on the GB10 (sm_121, triton 3.7.1, torch 2.13+cu130) at cce2aaadf3. `-k spec_verify`: 28 passed.

Kernel change from cce2aaa reverted, tests left as is: 3 failed (the new sliding-window test at window 8, 20, 40), 25 passed. So the new test catches it on sm_121 too.

Thanks, and good to know cce2aaa leaves the full-attention path alone. I'll run the new sliding-window test on gfx1201 when I next have a card free and post the result here.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to draft this comment.

Ran `cce2aaa` on gfx1201 as promised. Same setup as my earlier run (stock v0.31.1rc0 plus this PR, ROCm 10.0, torch 2.13, Triton 3.8.0), with the new commit applied on top.

`-k spec_verify`: 28 passed. With the `M` reset taken back out (kernel hunk reverted, new test kept), the three new cases fail and nothing else does:

| window | first failing `seq_len` | max abs diff |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 8 | 88 | 4.71 |
| 20 | 68 | 3.18 |
| 40 | 88 | 2.33 |

The rest of the file at the default `VLLM_TRITON_3D_MAX_Q=1` is still 1879 passed with the fix.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to run these measurements and draft this comment.

merged. Please rebase the PR, @SCcagg5.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

This is superseded by #56148, which landed on main after I opened this: it admits multi-token verify queries (up to `MAX_3D_QUERY_LEN = 8`) into the 3D split-KV path by default, and `softmax_step` / the reducer now keep an empty row's maximum at `-inf`.

Merging current main into this branch leaves only the `VLLM_TRITON_3D_MAX_Q` env var, which is no longer needed, so there is nothing left to review here. To be sure the hardening is equivalent, I ran this PR's three new test groups (reference match for q_len 2/4 with bf16 and fp8 KV, fully masked segment rows for seq_len 1..199, and the sliding-window masked-first-tile sweep with strongly negative logits) against main's kernel without any of the PR's changes: 28 passed (stock `v0.31.0` image with main's Python files, gfx1151).

Thanks @lobo235 for running it on gfx1201. Closing.

Thanks for following this through, and for the pointer to #56148. Glad the multi-token verify path landed on main with the empty-row hardening. We'll move our gfx1201 setup onto it and drop our local patch for the same routing.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

For multi-token sliding-window attention, a segment can start with a fully masked tile and later have valid keys. The first tile leaves `M=0, L=0`, so very negative scores in the next tile can underflow. This guard runs too late to recover the lost values.

@@ -632,6 +634,10 @@ def kernel_unified_attention(
                 acc,
                 mask=dim_mask[None, :] & query_mask_0[:, None] & query_mask_1[:, None],
             )
+        # With several query tokens per program, a row can
+        # have every key of this segment masked (ends at M = 0, L = 0). Report
+        # the segment as absent so reduce_segments ignores it.
+        M = tl.where(L > 0.0, M, float("-inf"))

nodes.body:
Good catch, you're right. I reproduced it: with a sliding window the loop starts at the window of the first token of the query block, so for a later token the first tile can be fully masked. `softmax_step` then leaves `M = 0, L = 0`, and if the logits of the next tile are below about -100 its keys underflow against that stale `M`; the epilogue guard sees `L = 0` and drops the segment.

It only happens when the window start falls in the last few positions of a tile, and the 2D path behaves the same, so it predates this PR, but this PR makes it reachable for sliding-window models during spec verify.

Fixed in cce2aaa: reset `M` to `-inf` while `L == 0` before `softmax_step`. New test `test_spec_verify_3d_sliding_window_masked_first_tile` (windows 8/20/40, strongly negative logits, 4 segments so a segment holds several tiles, sweep over `seq_len`). On gfx1151:

| kernel | new tests | full file (1667 cases) |
|---|---|---|
| previous head | 3 failed (max abs diff 3.1) | 1663 passed, 4 failed |
| with fix | 3 passed | 1666 passed, 1 failed |

The remaining failure is `test_softcap_does_not_overflow_on_large_scores`, which also fails on the unmodified v0.30.0 kernel on gfx1151. I left out the 240 `q_dtype1` / head 256 cases of `test_triton_unified_attn`: their Triton compile hangs on this machine with or without the change.

files.patch:
@@ -4,11 +4,11 @@
 
 import pytest
 import torch
-
 from vllm.platforms import current_platform
 from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
 from vllm.utils.math_utils import next_power_of_2
 from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_random_seed
+
 from vllm.v1.attention.ops.triton_attention_helpers import (
     apply_softcap,
     compute_tile_loop_bounds,
@@ -937,3 +937,117 @@ def test_softcap_does_not_overflow_on_large_scores() -> None:
     ref = soft_cap * torch.tanh(scores / soft_cap)
     assert torch.isfinite(out).all(), out
     torch.testing.assert_close(out, ref, atol=1e-3, rtol=1e-3)
+
+
+def _spec_verify_3d(
+    seq_len, q_len, block_size, kv_dtype, negative, window=None, segments=16
+):
+    """One causal multi-token query batch through the 3D path vs. a dense reference.
+
+    With ``negative`` all logits are strongly negative, so a row whose keys are
+    all masked in one segment must not report a finite segment maximum.
+    ``window`` enables sliding-window attention (each token sees ``window`` keys).
+    """
+    import vllm.v1.attention.ops.triton_unified_attention as ua
+
+    hq, hkv, d, threshold = 24, 4, 256, 32
+    nb = -(-seq_len // block_size) + 1
+    k = torch.randn(nb, block_size, hkv, d, device=DEVICE_TYPE, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    v = torch.randn_like(k)
+    q = torch.randn(q_len, hq, d, device=DEVICE_TYPE, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    if negative:
+        k, v, q = k.abs() + 1, v.abs() + 1, -8 * q.abs()
+    if kv_dtype is not None:
+        k, v = k.to(kv_dtype), v.to(kv_dtype)
+    block_table = (torch.randperm(nb - 1, device=DEVICE_TYPE) + 1).int()[None, :]
+    out = torch.empty_like(q)
+    ones = torch.ones(1, hkv, device=DEVICE_TYPE)
+    segm_out = torch.empty(threshold, hq, segments, d, device=DEVICE_TYPE)
+    segm_max = torch.empty(threshold, hq, segments, device=DEVICE_TYPE)
+    ua.unified_attention(
+        q=q,
+        k=k,
+        v=v,
+        out=out,
+        cu_seqlens_q=torch.tensor([0, q_len], dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE_TYPE),
+        max_seqlen_q=q_len,
+        seqused_k=torch.tensor([seq_len], dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE_TYPE),
+        max_seqlen_k=seq_len,
+        softmax_scale=d**-0.5,
+        causal=True,
+        window_size=(-1, -1) if window is None else (window - 1, 0),
+        block_table=block_table,
+        softcap=0,

+        softmax_segm_max=segm_max,
+        softmax_segm_expsum=torch.empty_like(segm_max),
+    )
+    keys = k[block_table[0].long()].float().reshape(-1, hkv, d)[:seq_len]
+    vals = v[block_table[0].long()].float().reshape(-1, hkv, d)[:seq_len]
+    keys = keys.repeat_interleave(hq // hkv, dim=1)
+    vals = vals.repeat_interleave(hq // hkv, dim=1)
+    scores = torch.einsum("qhd,khd->hqk", q.float(), keys) * d**-0.5
+    visible = seq_len - q_len + torch.arange(q_len, device=DEVICE_TYPE)[:, None]
+    pos = torch.arange(seq_len, device=DEVICE_TYPE)[None, :]

+    # Rows that see no key at all (seq_len < q_len) must come out as 0, not NaN.
+    ref = torch.einsum("hqk,khd->qhd", probs, vals)

inline_comments.body:
Good catch, you're right. I reproduced it: with a sliding window the loop starts at the window of the first token of the query block, so for a later token the first tile can be fully masked. `softmax_step` then leaves `M = 0, L = 0`, and if the logits of the next tile are below about -100 its keys underflow against that stale `M`; the epilogue guard sees `L = 0` and drops the segment.

It only happens when the window start falls in the last few positions of a tile, and the 2D path behaves the same, so it predates this PR, but this PR makes it reachable for sliding-window models during spec verify.

Fixed in cce2aaa: reset `M` to `-inf` while `L == 0` before `softmax_step`. New test `test_spec_verify_3d_sliding_window_masked_first_tile` (windows 8/20/40, strongly negative logits, 4 segments so a segment holds several tiles, sweep over `seq_len`). On gfx1151:

| kernel | new tests | full file (1667 cases) |
|---|---|---|
| previous head | 3 failed (max abs diff 3.1) | 1663 passed, 4 failed |
| with fix | 3 passed | 1666 passed, 1 failed |

The remaining failure is `test_softcap_does_not_overflow_on_large_scores`, which also fails on the unmodified v0.30.0 kernel on gfx1151. I left out the 240 `q_dtype1` / head 256 cases of `test_triton_unified_attn`: their Triton compile hangs on this machine with or without the change.

+        # have every key of this segment masked (ends at M = 0, L = 0). Report
+        # the segment as absent so reduce_segments ignores it.

Ran this on a DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121, CUDA 13) as a second platform for your gfx1151 numbers. **242 passed**, same as yours. Both guards are right and the gate default keeps today's behaviour.

One gap: **your test covers one of the two guards.** Ablating them separately:

```
both guards                        242 passed
reducer clamp removed              242 passed      <- not covered
epilogue -inf guard removed          1 failed, 241 passed
```

The clamp isn't redundant though — it's just unreachable from the sweep. `test_spec_verify_3d_masked_segment_sweep` runs `range(8, 521)` with `q_len=4`, so `context_len = seq_len - q_len >= 4` and every query row always sees at least one key. Going below that through your own `_run`:

```
q_len = 4, both guards        kv_len 1 2 3 4 5 8  ->  no NaN anywhere
q_len = 4, clamp removed      kv_len 1 2 3        ->  NaN
                              kv_len 4 5 8        ->  clean
```

So `kv_len < q_len` is the shape that needs it, and the sweep starts one step above it. Lowering the bound (or just adding `[1]` to the multi-sequence `seq_lens` set) would pin the clamp too — worth it because the clamp is the one that *looks* redundant next to the epilogue guard, so it's the one someone simplifies away later.

**Same pair, same order, on the DiffKV kernel.** #58141 carries the clamp and #59085 carried only the epilogue guard; on my card #59085 NaN'd at `q=8, kv_len=1` and `kv_len=3` until it picked up #58141's clamp, at which point those rows went to 0 and matched the 2D path exactly. Identical failure shape to what I just measured here, in the other file.
